The original article's subject position drew attention to the researcher, leaving the absence of evidence in a secondary clause. Subsequent checks showed that the results had been filed but indexed under a different project code. The correction should place the filing error first and name the person only where necessary. This change of information structure does not excuse withholding; it reflects the fact that withholding was not established at all. The correction will be displayed next to the archived article and linked from the updated version. The editor hopes that putting the verified filing facts first will make readers less likely to confuse an administrative classification error with a refusal to disclose information.

cases.passage_en: An audit summary compares two hospital wards that introduced different appointment reminder systems. Missed appointments fell on both wards, but the report did not control for seasonal staffing changes. One draft paragraph called the intervention a proven cause of the decline and then used this success to justify a separate claim about patient satisfaction, which the audit never measured. The editor's job is to repair the logical chain, keep the observed reduction in missed visits, and remove causal or experiential claims unsupported by the data. Clear cohesion should make the evidential boundary easier, not harder, to see. The report's limitations section also notes different appointment types and changes in staff availability across the wards. Without a suitable comparison design, those differences are plausible alternative explanations, not details that may be omitted for a smoother narrative conclusion.
